newsitem.title: MEXICO: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary -USDA.
newsitem.headline: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary -USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico were not sold in sufficient to establish trend preices this week.
Exports for the week were estimated at 6,000 head into Texas and New Mexico states, against 6,589 head last week and 973 head in the same week in 1996.

"Trade very slow, demand moderate. Bulk of supply consisted of medium and large steers weighing 300-600 lb. Around 40 percent of supply consisted of one lot of previously contracted yearlings weighing 600 lb which crossed at Santa Teresa, New Mexico," USDA said.
"A few lots of medium and large steers sold at 103 cents/lb base 300 lb," it added.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 93-103 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 83-93 cents/lb.
Imports into Mexico of slaughter cattle were estimated to have totaled 4,000 head for the week, it added. "Demand for slaughter cows remains very good in Mexico," it added.
